title: RAYE Announces One-Night Orchestral Show at Royal Albert Hall
excerpt: RAYE will perform her second album in full with an orchestra at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23 in a one-night concert.
body:
RAYE will perform her second album in full with an orchestra at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23 in a one-night concert. The show, titled *THIS SYMPHONY MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, will bring her band together with the Heritage Orchestra and Flames Collective choir. It reunites the singer with musicians behind her earlier symphonic performances, but the music will come from *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, released in March. Unlike her debut, the new record already incorporates orchestral music and big-band arrangements. RAYE worked with orchestral musicians on the studio recording, so some of the arrangements already have strings and brass at their centre.

The venue was the setting for her first large-scale symphonic concert in 2023. Backed by a 50-piece orchestra and choir, she performed songs from *My 21st Century Blues* in a show later released as *Live at the Royal Albert Hall*. The film was subsequently nominated for Best Music Film at the Grammy Awards. A sold-out concert at London's O2 in 2024 brought back the same orchestra and choir, with a programme again drawn from her debut album. The new concert returns to the Hall three years after the original performance, with an entirely different collection of songs to arrange.

Released in March, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* was conceived in four sections that RAYE calls seasons. It begins in a troubled place and moves through different styles and emotions toward a hopeful conclusion. The album moves between jazz, soul and cinematic orchestration, including "Click Clack Symphony.", a collaboration with Hans Zimmer. Elsewhere, intimate vocals give way to full-band performances, and the songs occasionally shift direction within the same track. For the Royal Albert Hall concert, those contrasts will be heard with a dedicated orchestra and choir rather than the changing instrumentation of the studio recordings.

RAYE has also released a new performance of "I Will Overcome." recorded at Abbey Road Studios. The video features the London Symphony Orchestra, which is not the ensemble announced for the upcoming concert. Rather than showing rehearsals from the Hall, it captures a separate studio session created alongside the announcement. The song appears immediately after the album's opening introduction, before the record moves into its different musical styles. She sings about living through painful experiences and finding the determination to carry on, a theme that returns elsewhere on the album. The video offers a full performance ahead of the October show, rather than a brief promotional trailer.

[youtube:Iy2FoVeIUXs]

This year's arena tour included six sold-out concerts at London's O2, with new songs performed alongside earlier favourites. RAYE later appeared as a guest on Bruno Mars' stadium dates in North America. She also brought "I Will Overcome." to the MTV Video Music Awards in September. The forthcoming concert will give the new record a different setting, with a full orchestra and choir accompanying her band for the evening. *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* became her first UK No. 1 album, while "WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!" passed one billion Spotify streams. The single's brassy chorus has a different feel from many of the longer arrangements that surround it on the album.

On the album, "WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!" arrives with several more songs still to play. One of them is "Joy.", which features RAYE's sisters, Amma and Absolutely, and celebrates the possibility of happiness after a difficult spell. The record closes with "Fin.", a six-minute composition that begins with RAYE directly addressing someone who has listened from the start. Her spoken words thank that person for staying with the music. Those spoken words are far removed from the brass-driven hit earlier on the album. At the Hall, the thank-you originally addressed to a listener will be part of a performance with a full orchestra, choir and an audience in front of her.
